reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the formation of Hf-rich interfacial precipitates, their role in hindering high-temperature deformation, and the improvement in high-temperature strength/ductility with unchanged room-temperature properties for the exact alloy system and Hf levels studied. However, the evidence does not mention density measurements, so the premise that density remains unaffected is unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Hf addition leads to Hf-rich precipitates at interfaces and inside B2 phase
Hf-rich precipitates hinder grain boundary sliding and dislocation movement at high temperature
High-temperature strength and ductility improve with Hf up to an optimum, then decline
Room-temperature mechanical properties remain almost unchanged with Hf addition
Trace Hf addition (~0.5 at.%) does not materially affect density
